  schedule_version varchar [note: 'Version number of this lifting schedule. Increments with each revision to track changes over the planning cycle as nominations are confirmed, vessels are assigned, or liftings are deferred.']
  tolerance_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The allowable percentage variance (plus or minus) from the nominated volume that is acceptable for this lifting.   total_planned_liftings varchar [note: 'The total number of individual cargo liftings planned for the period covered by this schedule. Used for capacity planning and logistics resource allocation.']
  total_planned_volume_bbl decimal(18,2) [note: 'The aggregate volume of all planned liftings for the period, measured in barrels (BBL). Represents the total crude oil or liquid hydrocarbon volume to be lifted across all cargoes in the schedule.']

  Note: 'Master planning entity governing FPSO and terminal crude oil liftings and the consolidated marine logistics schedule for a given planning horizon. Aligns with production sharing agreement (PSA) and joint operating agreement (JOA) lifting entitlements. Serves as the single operational master plan for marine logistics coordination, replacing separate shipping schedule and lifting program concepts.'
}

  demurrage_settlement_date date [note: 'Date when the demurrage claim was finally settled and payment was made or agreed.']

  despatch_hours decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total despatch hours earned when laytime used is less than laytime allowed. Despatch is a bonus paid by the shipowner to the charterer for saving time.']
  despatch_rate_per_day decimal(18,2) [note: 'Agreed daily rate for despatch payments, typically half the demurrage rate. Expressed in the freight currency.']
  fixture_date date [note: 'Date when the charter party agreement was fixed and agreed between the charterer and shipowner.']
  freight_currency varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the freight rate and voyage financial amounts.']
  freight_rate decimal(18,4) [note: 'The agreed freight rate for the voyage. Interpretation depends on freight_rate_basis (e.g., Worldscale points, lump sum amount, or per-unit rate).']
  freight_rate_basis varchar [note: 'Basis on which freight is calculated. Worldscale is a standard tanker rate index, lump sum is a fixed amount for the voyage, per-unit rates are based on cargo volume or weight.']
  governing_law varchar [note: 'The legal jurisdiction and law governing the charter party agreement (e.g., English Law, New York Law).']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this voyage record was last updated in the system.']
  laycan_end_date date [note: 'End date of the laycan window. If the vessel does not arrive by this date, the charterer may have the right to cancel the charter.']
  laycan_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the laycan (laydays and canceling) window. The earliest date the vessel is expected to arrive at the load port.']
  payment_terms varchar [note: 'Terms and conditions for freight payment, including timing, method, and any advance or retention clauses.']
  port_charges_total decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total port charges incurred across all port calls during the voyage, including port dues, pilotage, tugs, and agency fees. Expressed in freight currency.']
  profit_loss decimal(18,2) [note: 'Net profit or loss for the voyage, calculated as freight revenue minus voyage costs (bunker, port charges, canal fees, demurrage/despatch net). Expressed in freight currency. Business-confidential financial metric.']
  total_laytime_allowed_hours decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total laytime (loading and discharge time) allowed under the charter party terms, expressed in hours. Laytime is the time allowed for cargo operations.']
  total_laytime_used_hours decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total laytime actually used across all load and discharge ports, expressed in hours. Calculated from port call records.']
  voyage_number varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the voyage, typically assigned by the commercial or operations team. Used for external communication and documentation.']
  voyage_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of the voyage. Tracks the voyage lifecycle from planning through completion or cancellation.']

  Note: 'Transactional record representing a vessel\'s complete commercial and operational journey from fixture to settlement. Captures voyage number, vessel ID, charter party terms (charter type, fixture date, charterer, shipowner, freight rate basis — Worldscale or lump sum, governing law, payment terms), laycan, port call sequence (load/discharge/bunker ports with ETA, ATA, NOR tendered, berthing, operations commencement/completion, departure, port agent, PDA, port state control results), commencement and completion of loading/discharge, total laytime used per port, demurrage or despatch hours and rates, demurrage claim details (claim reference, claim amount, claim status — draft/submitted/disputed/agreed/settled, counterparty, dispute reason, settlement date), freight rate, voyage status, and voyage P&L. Serves as the single lifecycle record integrating charter party terms, port calls, laytime statements, demurrage claims, and freight invoicing.'
}

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this freight invoice record was first created in the system.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the freight invoice is denominated. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USD|EUR|GBP|CAD|AUD|JPY|CNY — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  demurrage_charge decimal(18,2) [note: 'Additional charge assessed for delays in loading or unloading beyond the agreed laytime, typically applicable to marine vessel and truck transportation.']
  despatch_credit decimal(18,2) [note: 'Credit issued to the shipper for completing loading or unloading operations faster than the agreed laytime, reducing the total invoice amount.']
  destination_location varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the destination location where the freight was delivered (refinery, terminal, port, or delivery point).']
  dispute_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this freight invoice is under dispute due to billing discrepancies, service quality issues, or contractual disagreements.']
  dispute_reason varchar [note: 'Description of the reason for the invoice dispute, such as incorrect volume, rate discrepancy, or service quality issue.']
  freight_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'Unit freight rate charged by the carrier per the rate basis (e.g., dollars per barrel, dollars per MCF).']
  freight_rate_basis varchar [note: 'Basis on which the freight rate is calculated: per barrel, per MCF, per ton, per mile, lump sum, or worldscale (for tanker charters).']
  fuel_surcharge decimal(18,2) [note: 'Additional charge to cover fluctuations in fuel costs, typically applied to truck and rail transportation.']
  invoice_date date [note: 'Date the freight invoice was issued by the carrier or freight broker.']
  invoice_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique invoice number issued by the carrier or freight broker for this transportation service billing document.']
  invoice_receipt_date date [note: 'Date the freight invoice was received by the accounts payable department for processing.']
  invoice_status varchar [note: 'Current processing status of the freight invoice in the accounts payable workflow: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, processed, or cancelled.']
  jib_allocation_status varchar [note: 'Status of allocation of this freight invoice cost to joint venture partners under Joint Interest Billing (JIB) arrangements: pending, allocated, completed, or not applicable.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this freight invoice record was last modified or updated.']
  origin_location varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the origin location where the freight movement originated (production facility, terminal, port, or custody transfer point).']
  paid_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total amount paid to date against this freight invoice, supporting partial payment tracking.']
  payment_date date [note: 'Actual date the freight invoice was paid or partially paid.']
  payment_due_date date [note: 'Date by which payment is due to the carrier per the payment terms.']
  payment_status varchar [note: 'Current payment status of the freight invoice: pending, paid, partial (partially paid), overdue, disputed, or cancelled.']
  payment_terms varchar [note: 'Payment terms specified on the invoice, such as Net 30, Net 60, or Due on Receipt.']
  pda_charge decimal(18,2) [note: 'Port disbursement account charges covering port fees, pilotage, tugs, and other port-related expenses incurred during marine vessel operations.']

  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Mode of transportation used for the freight movement: pipeline, tanker (marine vessel), truck, rail, barge, or FPSO (Floating Production Storage and Offloading).']
  volume_unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the shipped volume: BBL (barrels), MCF (thousand cubic feet), MMCF (million cubic feet), GAL (gallons), MT (metric tons), M3 (cubic meters).']

  Note: 'Transactional billing document issued by a carrier or freight broker to the shipper for transportation services rendered across all transport modes. Captures invoice number, invoice date, carrier ID, voyage or shipment reference, transport mode, freight rate basis, base freight amount, demurrage charges, despatch credits, port disbursement account (PDA) charges, fuel surcharge, currency, payment due date, payment status, dispute flag, and cost allocation to specific cargoes and cost centers. Supports accounts payable processing, freight cost management, and carrier performance tracking.'
}

  metered_delivery_volume decimal(18,3) [note: 'Volume measured at the delivery meter point, used for custody transfer reconciliation and volume accounting.']
  metered_receipt_volume decimal(18,3) [note: 'Volume measured at the receipt/injection meter point, used for custody transfer and shipper allocation calculations.']

  rvp_psi decimal(6,2) [note: 'Reid Vapor Pressure measurement in PSI for gasoline and light products, used for quality control and safety compliance.']
  scada_integration_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this batch is integrated with SCADA systems for real-time monitoring and control.']
  shrinkage_volume decimal(18,3) [note: 'Volume reduction due to temperature and pressure changes, phase transitions, or processing losses during transportation.']
  sulfur_content_percent decimal(6,4) [note: 'Percentage of sulfur content in the product, critical for quality specification compliance and environmental regulations.']

  tariff_rate_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the tariff rate (e.g., USD per barrel, USD per MMBTU).']
  volume_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for all actual volume measurements in this batch record. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BBL|MBBL|MMCF|BCF|MCF|GAL|M3 — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Transactional record representing a discrete batch of petroleum product injected into and transported through a pipeline system, including throughput measurement, shipper allocation, and volume reconciliation. Captures batch ID, pipeline segment ID, batch sequence number, product type and grade, shipper ID, injection and delivery points, injection start/end timestamps, nominated volume (BBL or MMCFD), actual injected volume, metered receipt and delivery volumes, daily and monthly throughput aggregations, line loss or gain, fuel gas used, shrinkage, imbalance volume, batch quality specifications (API gravity, sulfur content, RVP), interface management instructions, measurement point references, and batch status. Supports pipeline scheduling, quality tracking, shipper allocation, shipper imbalance management, FERC Form 6 reporting, and tariff revenue calculation. Serves as the SSOT for all pipeline volume tracking from nomination fulfillment through delivery reconciliation.'

Table logistics.pipeline_throughput {
  pipeline_throughput_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the pipeline throughput record. Primary key for this transactional entity capturing daily or monthly measured volumes on pipeline segments.']

Simultaneously, each customer counterparty typically has access agreements with multiple terminals across different geographic locations to support their supply chain network. These are formal commercial arrangements with customer-specific terms including allocated capacity, priority levels, tariff overrides, and nomination rights that cannot be stored on either the terminal or customer entity alone.'

Each carrier operates under carrier-specific rates, volume allocations, and service level agreements within the same master contract. Conversely, a single carrier typically provides services under multiple term contracts serving different customers, routes, or product types. This is an operational procurement pattern where logistics teams actively manage carrier engagements, track performance against contract-specific SLAs, and optimize multi-carrier sourcing strategies.'
}

  nomination_lead_days varchar [note: 'Minimum number of calendar days in advance that a delivery nomination must be submitted for this delivery point. Drives nomination management workflows in Avocet Production Operations and SAP SD scheduling. Ensures operational readiness and regulatory compliance.']
  norm_risk_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this delivery point has identified Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM) risk associated with produced water, scale, or sludge handling. NORM-flagged locations require specialized waste management, personnel monitoring, and regulatory reporting per EPA and state radiation control programs.']
  offshore_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the delivery point is located offshore (True) or onshore (False). Offshore delivery points are subject to BSEE/BOEM regulatory oversight, additional HSE requirements, and FPSO/marine logistics protocols.']
  operating_hours varchar [note: 'Description of the delivery point\'s operational hours (e.g., \'24/7\', \'Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00 Local\', \'Daylight hours only\'). Used for logistics scheduling, nomination window management, and customer delivery planning.']
  operational_status varchar [note: 'Current operational lifecycle state of the delivery point. Controls whether the location is available for nomination and scheduling. \'suspended\' indicates temporary unavailability; \'decommissioned\' indicates permanent retirement from service.']
  pipeline_system_name varchar [note: 'Name of the pipeline system or network to which this delivery point is connected (e.g., \'Colonial Pipeline\', \'Trans-Alaska Pipeline System\'). Applicable for pipeline_interconnect and terminal delivery point types. Used for tariff determination and FERC/PHMSA regulatory reporting.']
  postal_code varchar [note: 'Postal or ZIP code for the delivery point location. Used for logistics routing, tax jurisdiction determination, and regulatory compliance filings.']
  region varchar [note: 'Business-defined geographic region or operating area in which the delivery point is located (e.g., \'Gulf Coast\', \'North Sea\', \'Middle East\', \'Asia Pacific\'). Used for regional logistics planning, commercial reporting, and supply chain segmentation.']
  regulatory_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this delivery point (e.g., \'FERC\', \'BSEE\', \'EPA Region 6\', \'PHMSA\', \'UK HSE\'). Determines applicable safety, environmental, and operational compliance requirements. Used for regulatory reporting and permit management.']
  state_province varchar [note: 'State, province, or administrative subdivision where the delivery point is located. Required for regulatory jurisdiction mapping (e.g., state environmental permits, PHMSA state pipeline safety programs) and tax/royalty reporting.']
  storage_capacity_bbl decimal(18,3) [note: 'Maximum storage capacity of the delivery point facility expressed in barrels (BBL). Principal quantitative fact for storage facilities, terminals, and FPSOs. Used for inventory planning, nomination management, and capacity allocation. Applicable to crude oil, NGL, LPG, and refined product locations.']
  tariff_code varchar [note: 'Applicable pipeline or terminal tariff code governing the transportation or throughput charges at this delivery point. Used for freight cost calculation, FERC tariff compliance, and SAP SD pricing condition determination.']
  throughput_capacity_bopd decimal(18,3) [note: 'Maximum throughput or loading/discharge rate of the delivery point expressed in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD). Used for logistics scheduling, nomination management, and capacity constraint modeling. Applicable to terminals, racks, pipeline interconnects, and refinery gates.']
  time_zone varchar [note: 'IANA time zone identifier for the delivery point location (e.g., \'America/Chicago\', \'Europe/Amsterdam\', \'Asia/Riyadh\'). Used to correctly interpret operating hours, nomination deadlines, and delivery timestamps in logistics and scheduling systems.']
  unlocode varchar [note: 'UN/LOCODE five-character code identifying the port, terminal, or logistics location (e.g., USGLS for Galveston, NLRTM for Rotterdam). Mandatory for international trade documentation, LNG/LPG cargo nominations, and customs declarations. Aligns with UNECE Trade Facilitation standards.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this delivery point record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  water_depth_m decimal(10,2) [note: 'Water depth in metres at the offshore delivery point location. Applicable only to offshore berths, FPSO offloading points, and subsea pipeline interconnects. Used for vessel compatibility assessment and marine logistics planning.']

  Note: 'Physical or logical delivery location associated with a customer account, including terminal name, port of loading/discharge, pipeline interconnect point, rack location, refinery gate, storage facility, geographic coordinates, country, region, delivery mode (pipeline, tanker, truck, rail), UNLOCODE, and operational status. Supports logistics scheduling, nomination management, and product delivery execution for crude oil, LNG, LPG, NGL, and refined product customers.'
}

  risk_tier varchar [note: 'Internal risk tier classification for the counterparty, used to apply differentiated credit policies, collateral requirements, and monitoring intensity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CREDIT_LIMIT_CHANGE|RATING_CHANGE|COLLATERAL_CALL|CREDIT_HOLD|CREDIT_RELEASE|PAYMENT_DEFAULT|CREDIT_REVIEW_COMPLETED|CREDIT_WATCH|COVENANT_BREACH|MARGIN_CALL — promote to reference product]']

  kyc_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty\'s Know Your Customer (KYC) verification was current and valid at the time of this credit event.   new_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The updated value of the credit attribute after this event is applied. Stores the after-state for audit trail purposes. Stored as STRING to accommodate heterogeneous event types.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional commentary, context, or instructions related to this credit event. May include analyst observations, counterparty communications summary, escalation notes, or remediation actions. Supports credit review documentation and audit trail completeness.']
  payment_default_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary value of the overdue or defaulted payment that triggered a PAYMENT_DEFAULT credit event. Represents the outstanding invoice amount not paid within contractual terms. Null for non-default events.']
  previous_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The prior value of the credit attribute before this event was applied. Stores the before-state for audit trail purposes. For CREDIT_LIMIT_CHANGE, this is the prior limit amount as a string; for RATING_CHANGE, this is the prior rating code (e.g., \'BBB+\'); for CREDIT_HOLD, this is the prior status. Stored as STRING to accommodate heterogeneous event types.']
  rating_agency varchar [note: 'The source of the credit rating referenced in this event. Null for non-rating events.']
  rating_new varchar [note: 'The credit rating code assigned to the counterparty after this rating change event (e.g., \'BB+\', \'Ba1\', \'BBB-\'). Follows the rating scale of the designated rating_agency. Null for non-rating events.']
  rating_previous varchar [note: 'The credit rating code assigned to the counterparty before this rating change event (e.g., \'BBB+\', \'Baa1\', \'A-\'). Follows the rating scale of the designated rating_agency. Null for non-rating events.']
  reversal_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this credit event has been reversed (True) due to error, dispute resolution, or system correction. When True, the reversed_event_id field identifies the original event being reversed. Supports SOX audit trail integrity.']
  review_due_date date [note: 'The scheduled date by which the next credit review must be completed following this event. Drives credit review workflow and ensures periodic reassessment of counterparty creditworthiness in accordance with credit policy. Particularly important after CREDIT_HOLD or RATING_CHANGE events.']
  sanctions_screened boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty was screened against applicable sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Sanctions) at the time of this credit event. Required for regulatory compliance in international oil and gas trading operations.']
  source_document_number varchar [note: 'The document number in the originating source system (e.g., SAP FI document number, trading system transaction ID) that corresponds to this credit event. Enables cross-system traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and operational systems of record.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The originating system that generated or recorded this credit event. SAP_FI: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting Credit Management module; MANUAL: manually entered by credit analyst; TRADING_SYSTEM: generated by commodity trading and risk management system; EXTERNAL_FEED: received from external credit bureau or rating agency data feed.']
  trigger_category varchar [note: 'Structured classification of the root cause category that triggered this credit event. Enables trend analysis and portfolio-level credit risk reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PAYMENT_BEHAVIOR|EXTERNAL_RATING|FINANCIAL_DETERIORATION|MARKET_CONDITIONS|PERIODIC_REVIEW|COVENANT_BREACH|REGULATORY|COUNTERPARTY_REQUEST|COLLATERAL_SHORTFALL — promote to reference product]']
  trigger_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the business reason or triggering condition that caused this credit event. Examples include: \'Counterparty missed payment on crude oil invoice #INV-2024-001234\', \'External rating downgrade by S&P from BBB to BB+\', \'Commodity price volatility increased mark-to-market exposure beyond threshold\', \'Annual credit review completed\'. Required for SOX audit trail.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this credit event record was last modified in the system. Tracks subsequent updates such as status changes, approval completions, or reversal processing. Required for data lineage and SOX audit trail in the Databricks Lakehouse silver layer.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of credit-related events affecting a counterparty\'s credit profile, including credit limit changes, credit rating downgrades/upgrades, collateral calls, credit holds, credit releases, payment defaults, and credit review completions. Captures event type, event date, previous value, new value, triggering reason, approving authority, and associated exposure amount. Provides full audit trail for credit risk management and SOX compliance.'

  beneficial_ownership_disclosed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty has fully disclosed its ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 25% or more ownership interest, as required under FATF Recommendation 24 and FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule. Mandatory for all trading counterparties.']
  counterparty_legal_name varchar [note: 'Full registered legal name of the counterparty as recorded in official corporate documents and used for KYC identity verification. Applies to IOCs, NOCs, refiners, traders, wholesale buyers, and other commercial counterparties.']
  counterparty_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the counterparty by business role in the oil and gas value chain. Distinguishes between International Oil Companies (IOCs), National Oil Companies (NOCs), refiners, traders, wholesale buyers, industrial consumers, retail distributors, and contract counterparties. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IOC|NOC|refiner|trader|wholesale_buyer|industrial_consumer|retail_distributor|contract_counterparty — promote to reference product]']
  country_of_incorporation varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction where the counterparty is legally incorporated or registered. Used for sanctions screening, OFAC/EU/UN list matching, and jurisdictional risk assessment.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this KYC record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail anchor for the record\'s lifecycle and supports SOX compliance audit requirements.']
  credit_risk_linked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this KYC record has been linked to an active credit risk assessment and credit limit in the credit management system. KYC approval is a prerequisite for credit limit assignment for trading counterparties.']
  document_collection_status varchar [note: 'Status of the collection of required KYC documentation from the counterparty, including certificate of incorporation, articles of association, beneficial ownership declarations, financial statements, and authorized signatory lists. Incomplete documentation blocks trading approval.']
  document_expiry_date date [note: 'Earliest expiry date among the key KYC documents collected for this counterparty (e.g., certificate of good standing, trade license). When any document expires, the document_collection_status must be updated and renewal initiated.']
  eu_sanctions_screening_result varchar [note: 'Result of screening the counterparty against the European Union consolidated sanctions list. Mandatory for all EU-jurisdiction trading activities and European counterparties. A confirmed match prohibits transactions under EU law.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the current KYC record expires and a renewal review is required. Determined by KYC tier: Enhanced Due Diligence records typically expire annually, Standard every two years, Simplified every three years per internal compliance policy.']
  fatf_framework_version varchar [note: 'Version of the FATF Recommendations framework under which this KYC record was prepared and assessed (e.g., FATF 2012 Revised Recommendations, FATF 2023 Update). Ensures traceability of compliance assessments to the applicable regulatory standard version.']
  jurisdiction_risk_rating varchar [note: 'Risk classification of the counterparty\'s country of incorporation based on FATF grey/black lists, OFAC sanctioned country lists, and internal country risk policy. Drives KYC tier assignment and enhanced due diligence requirements.']
  kyc_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this KYC compliance record, used for audit trails, regulatory submissions, and compliance officer tracking. Format: KYC- followed by alphanumeric characters.']
  kyc_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the KYC compliance record indicating whether the counterparty has passed, is under review, or has failed the KYC process. Drives trading eligibility and credit decisions.']
  kyc_tier varchar [note: 'Classification of the level of due diligence applied to this counterparty. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to high-risk counterparties such as state-owned NOCs, PEPs, or entities in high-risk jurisdictions. Standard applies to typical IOC/trading counterparties. Simplified applies to low-risk, regulated entities.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent periodic KYC review was completed. Distinct from verification_date (initial verification) and next_review_date (scheduled future review). Used to track review cadence compliance and identify overdue reviews.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next periodic KYC review. May differ from expiry_date if an interim review is triggered by a risk event, sanctions alert, or change in counterparty ownership structure.']
  ofac_screening_result varchar [note: 'Result of screening the counterparty against the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Blocked Persons List. A confirmed match prohibits all transactions. Potential matches require compliance officer review.']
  onboarding_date date [note: 'Date on which the counterparty was first onboarded into the KYC compliance program. Represents the start of the commercial relationship from a compliance perspective and anchors the KYC lifecycle timeline.']
  pep_category varchar [note: 'Specific category of PEP classification when pep_flag is true. Distinguishes between domestic PEPs (e.g., government ministers), foreign PEPs (e.g., heads of state), international organization PEPs, close associates, and family members. Relevant for NOC counterparties with government-affiliated executives.']
  pep_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty or any of its beneficial owners is classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) — a current or former senior government official, state-owned enterprise executive, or close associate. PEP status mandates Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) per FATF Recommendation 12.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the reason for KYC rejection when kyc_status is \'rejected\'. Documents the specific compliance deficiency, sanctions match, or documentation failure that resulted in rejection. Required for audit trail and regulatory reporting.']
  review_trigger varchar [note: 'Reason that initiated the most recent KYC review. Distinguishes between scheduled periodic reviews and event-driven reviews triggered by sanctions alerts, changes in beneficial ownership, adverse media findings, risk escalations, or regulatory requests.']
  risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric composite risk score (0.00–100.00) calculated from the weighted combination of jurisdiction risk, AML risk rating, PEP status, sanctions exposure, adverse media findings, and beneficial ownership complexity. Higher scores indicate greater compliance risk. Used to prioritize enhanced due diligence and monitoring resources.']
  sanctions_screening_date date [note: 'Most recent date on which the counterparty was screened against OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions lists. Sanctions screening must be refreshed at defined intervals and upon any material change in counterparty ownership or jurisdiction.']
  source_system_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier of this KYC record in the originating compliance management system (e.g., Enablon HSE Management or dedicated KYC platform). Enables traceability from the Silver layer back to the operational system of record for audit and reconciliation purposes.']
  trading_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty is currently eligible for crude oil, natural gas, LNG, NGL, or refined product trading based on the current KYC status, sanctions screening results, AML risk rating, and document collection completeness. Set to false when KYC is expired, rejected, or sanctions match is confirmed.']
  ubo_count varchar [note: 'Number of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) identified and disclosed for this counterparty. A UBO is any natural person holding 25% or more direct or indirect ownership or control. Used to assess ownership complexity and completeness of beneficial ownership disclosure.']
  un_sanctions_screening_result varchar [note: 'Result of screening the counterparty against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list. Applies globally to all counterparties regardless of jurisdiction. A confirmed match prohibits all transactions under international law.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this KYC record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Updated on every status change, review completion, sanctions screening refresh, or document update. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.']
  verification_date date [note: 'Date on which the KYC verification process was completed and the counterparty\'s identity and documentation were confirmed by the compliance team. Marks the start of the KYC validity period.']
  waiver_expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the compliance waiver expires when waiver_flag is true. After this date, trading eligibility is automatically suspended until full KYC compliance is restored. Null when no waiver is in effect.']
  waiver_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a formal compliance waiver has been granted for this KYC record, allowing temporary trading eligibility despite incomplete documentation or pending review. Waivers require senior compliance authority approval and are time-limited.']

  Note: 'Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance record for each counterparty, capturing KYC status, verification date, KYC tier (enhanced due diligence, standard, simplified), beneficial ownership disclosure, sanctions screening result (OFAC, EU, UN), politically exposed person (PEP) flag, anti-money laundering (AML) risk rating, document collection status, KYC expiry date, compliance officer, and next review date. Mandatory for all trading counterparties under FATF, OFAC, and internal compliance frameworks.'
}

Business justification: Pricing formulas and index preferences require commercial manager approval before contract execution. Regulatory requirement in many jurisdictions for price risk management. approved_by is denormalize']
  commercial_term_contract_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the commercial contract or sales agreement under which this pricing index preference applies. Supports back-office settlement and deal structuring.']
  customer_counterparty_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer account for which this price index preference is configured. Links to the customer master record in the SSOT customer domain.']
  joa_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: JOA partners may elect specific pricing bases for their equity crude offtake. Enables JOA partner-specific pricing elections, equity crude pricing administration, and partner commercial terms manageme']
  petroleum_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Price index preferences specify pricing formulas for specific petroleum products (crude grades, refined products, NGLs). Commercial teams configure product-specific pricing differentials and indices f']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'The commercial approval workflow status for this pricing index preference. \'draft\' indicates under preparation; \'pending_approval\' indicates submitted for commercial review; \'approved\' indicates authorized for use in contracts; \'rejected\' indicates not approved; \'withdrawn\' indicates recalled by the submitter.']
  approved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this pricing index preference was formally approved by the authorized commercial manager. Supports audit trail, SOX compliance, and contract lifecycle management.']
  ceiling_price_usd decimal(18,6) [note: 'The maximum price per unit (in the differential_unit currency) above which the effective price will not rise, regardless of the benchmark index movement. Provides price protection for the buyer in volatile market conditions. Expressed in the same unit as differential_usd.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this price index preference record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the price index and differential are denominated. Typically USD for international crude oil and products trading. Supports multi-currency commercial agreements and financial settlement.']
  delivery_location_code varchar [note: 'The standardized code identifying the delivery point or terminal associated with this pricing preference (e.g., Cushing OK for WTI, Rotterdam for Brent products). Aligns the pricing basis with the physical delivery location for FOB/CIF/DES pricing.']
  differential_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the pricing differential. USD per barrel (USD/BBL) for crude oil and liquid products; USD per MMBTU for natural gas and LNG; USD per metric ton (USD/MT) for petrochemicals; USD per thousand cubic feet (USD/MCF) or USD per gigajoule (USD/GJ) for gas contracts.']
  differential_usd decimal(18,6) [note: 'The premium or discount applied to the benchmark price index, expressed in USD per barrel (BBL) for crude oil and refined products, or USD per MMBTU for natural gas.   effective_until date [note: 'The date on which this price index preference expires and is no longer applicable. Nullable for open-ended preferences. Supports contract pricing configuration and temporal validity management.']

  floor_price_usd decimal(18,6) [note: 'The minimum price per unit (in the differential_unit currency) below which the effective price will not fall, regardless of the benchmark index movement. Provides price protection for the seller in volatile market conditions. Expressed in the same unit as differential_usd.']
  geographic_region varchar [note: 'The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary geographic region or destination country associated with this pricing preference. Used for regional pricing analytics, regulatory compliance, and export/import pricing differentiation.']
  index_grade varchar [note: 'The specific crude oil grade or product specification associated with the benchmark index (e.g., \'WTI Cushing\', \'Dated Brent\', \'Dubai Fateh\', \'Arab Light\', \'Urals\'). Provides granularity beyond the index code for precise commercial and settlement purposes.']
  index_publication_source varchar [note: 'The authoritative price reporting agency or exchange that publishes the benchmark index used for pricing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PLATTS|ARGUS|ICIS|OPIS|REUTERS|BLOOMBERG|ICE|NYMEX|CME — promote to reference product]']
  is_formula_based boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this preference uses a complex formula expression (TRUE) rather than a simple index-plus-differential structure (FALSE). When TRUE, the pricing_formula field contains the authoritative pricing expression.']
  is_provisional_pricing boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pricing preference uses provisional pricing (TRUE) with subsequent final price adjustment, or direct final pricing (FALSE).   market_segment varchar [note: 'The commercial market segment classification for this pricing preference.   notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing additional commercial context, special conditions, negotiation notes, or exceptions associated with this pricing index preference. Not used for formula expressions (see pricing_formula).']
  preference_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable label or short description identifying this pricing index preference configuration, used for display in commercial deal structuring and contract management interfaces.']
  preference_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the price index preference record. \'active\' indicates the preference is in use for pricing; \'pending\' indicates awaiting approval; \'expired\' indicates past the effective period; \'superseded\' indicates replaced by a newer preference.']
  price_index_code varchar [note: 'The preferred benchmark price index used for pricing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WTI|BRENT|DUBAI|PLATTS|ARGUS|HENRY_HUB|NBP|JKM|OPIS|ICE — promote to reference product]']
  price_index_description varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the benchmark price index, providing additional context beyond the code (e.g., \'West Texas Intermediate Cushing Oklahoma\', \'Dated Brent North Sea\'). Supports reporting and contract documentation.']
  pricing_basis varchar [note: 'The delivery and pricing basis (Incoterms) agreed with the customer.   pricing_formula varchar [note: 'The full pricing formula expression as defined in the commercial contract, capturing complex multi-index blends, conditional differentials, or formula-based pricing structures (e.g., \'0.5 * WTI + 0.5 * BRENT - 1.50\'). Supports advanced deal structuring beyond simple index plus differential configurations.']
  pricing_frequency varchar [note: 'The frequency at which the price index is re-evaluated or re-set for ongoing supply agreements. \'daily\' for spot-linked contracts; \'monthly\' for term contracts using monthly average indices; \'quarterly\' for longer-term supply agreements.']
  pricing_period_type varchar [note: 'Defines the pricing period convention for determining the applicable benchmark price. \'month_of_loading\' uses the average index price during the cargo loading month; \'month_after_loading\' uses the following month; \'average_of_period\' uses a defined averaging window; \'spot\' uses the day-of-transaction price; \'custom\' uses a bespoke period defined in the contract.']
  provisional_price_usd decimal(18,6) [note: 'The provisional or estimated price per unit used for initial invoicing before the final benchmark index price is published and the settlement lag period has elapsed. Common in crude oil trading where final prices are determined after cargo delivery.']
  quotation_period_days varchar [note: 'The number of consecutive business days over which the benchmark price index is averaged to determine the final settlement price. Commonly 5, 10, or 20 days. Used in conjunction with pricing_period_type to define the exact price averaging window for back-office settlement.']
  quotation_period_start_offset varchar [note: 'The number of days before or after the bill of lading date (or loading date) at which the quotation period begins. A negative value indicates the period starts before the loading date; a positive value indicates it starts after. Used to precisely define the price averaging window relative to the cargo event.']
  secondary_index_code varchar [note: 'An optional secondary benchmark price index used in blended or multi-index pricing formulas (e.g., a 50/50 blend of WTI and Brent). Populated only when is_formula_based is TRUE and the formula references a second index.']
  secondary_index_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'The weighting factor (0.0000 to 1.0000) applied to the secondary price index in a blended pricing formula. For example, 0.5000 represents a 50% weighting. The primary index weight is implied as (1 - secondary_index_weight).']
  settlement_lag_days varchar [note: 'The number of calendar days after the pricing period end date before the final invoice price is settled and invoiced. Accounts for the time required to obtain final published index prices and complete back-office settlement calculations.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this pricing index preference record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse. Examples: SAP_SD (SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution), AVOCET (Avocet Production Operations), MANUAL (manually entered), PLATTS_API (Platts data feed), ARGUS_API (Argus data feed).']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'The primary mode of transportation associated with this pricing preference and delivery basis. Relevant for determining applicable freight adjustments and logistics cost components in the pricing structure.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this price index preference record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse.']
  volume_max_bbl decimal(18,3) [note: 'The maximum transaction volume in barrels (BBL) or barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) for which this pricing index preference is applicable. Nullable for unlimited upper bound. Supports tiered pricing structures.']
  volume_min_bbl decimal(18,3) [note: 'The minimum transaction volume in barrels (BBL) or barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) for which this pricing index preference is applicable. Supports tiered pricing structures where different index preferences apply at different volume thresholds.']

  Note: 'Customer-level pricing index preferences and benchmark configurations, capturing preferred price index (WTI, Brent, Dubai, Platts, Argus), pricing basis (FOB, CIF, DES, DAP), differential (premium/discount in USD/BBL or USD/MMBTU), pricing period (month of loading, month after loading), quotation period, and applicable product category. Supports commercial deal structuring, contract pricing configuration, and back-office settlement for crude oil and products trading.'

  pricing_basis varchar [note: 'The benchmark price index against which the nominated cargo will be priced per the contract terms (e.g., Dated Brent, WTI Cushing, Platts Dubai, NYMEX Natural Gas). Drives price calculation at bill of lading date or delivery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dated_brent|wti_cushing|platts_dubai|argus_sour|nymex_ng|ice_brent — promote to reference product]']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the nomination, used in communications with the customer, terminal operators, and logistics teams. Follows the NOM- prefix convention.']

  sanctions_screened boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer, vessel, and destination country have been screened against OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions lists prior to nomination confirmation. Must be True before confirmation_timestamp is populated.']
  shipper_code varchar [note: 'The FERC-assigned or pipeline operator-assigned code identifying the shipper of record for pipeline nominations. Required for FERC-regulated interstate pipeline capacity scheduling and balancing.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this nomination record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.   tolerance_max_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum allowable percentage above the nominated volume that may be delivered without requiring a separate nomination amendment. Expressed as a positive percentage (e.g., 5.00 for 5% over).']
  tolerance_min_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The minimum allowable percentage below the nominated volume that the customer may accept at delivery without triggering a contract shortfall or take-or-pay obligation. Expressed as a negative percentage (e.g., -5.00 for 5% under).']

  volume_boe decimal(18,4) [note: 'Nominated volume converted to Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE) for cross-commodity comparison, portfolio reporting, and SEC reserves disclosure alignment. Conversion factors applied per API/SPE standards.']
  volume_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure in which the nominated volume is expressed. BBL (barrels) for crude and liquid products, MT (metric tonnes) for LNG and bulk cargoes, MMBTU for natural gas, MCF/MMCF for pipeline gas volumes, M3 for metric volume reporting.']

  Note: 'Customer delivery nomination record capturing the formal request by a customer to lift or receive a cargo or pipeline volume under a term contract or spot sale. Core operational record linking customer demand to logistics scheduling, vessel chartering, and terminal operations.'

  lifting_tolerance_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Contractual tolerance percentage (e.g., ±5%) applied to the entitlement volume within which the actual lifted volume is considered compliant with the offtake agreement. Volumes outside this tolerance may trigger over/under-lift balancing obligations.']
  net_standard_volume decimal(18,4) [note: 'Gross standard volume minus the volume of sediment, water, and free water (BS&W deductions) at standard conditions. Represents the net merchantable hydrocarbon volume for invoicing, revenue recognition, and production allocation reporting.']
  nomination_deadline date [note: 'Contractual deadline by which the buyer must nominate the lifting vessel to the seller or terminal operator. Failure to nominate by this date may result in forfeiture of the lifting entitlement or deferral under the offtake agreement terms.']
  over_under_lift_status varchar [note: 'Classification of the lifting outcome relative to entitlement: over_lift (actual > entitlement + tolerance), under_lift (actual < entitlement - tolerance), balanced (within tolerance), or pending (lifting not yet completed). Drives JOA partner balancing and make-up lifting obligations.']
  price_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the cargo price and invoice are denominated (e.g., USD for US Dollar, EUR for Euro). Most international crude oil and LNG trades are denominated in USD.']
  price_differential decimal(10,4) [note: 'Contractual premium or discount applied to the reference pricing basis for this cargo, expressed in USD per BBL or USD per MT. Reflects crude quality differentials, location adjustments, and commercial negotiation outcomes. Confidential commercial term.']
  pricing_basis varchar [note: 'Reference price benchmark against which the cargo price is calculated (e.g., Dated Brent, WTI, Dubai/Oman, Platts Oman, JKM for LNG). Determines the pricing formula applied for revenue recognition and invoice generation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dated_brent|wti|dubai_oman|platts_oman|argus_sour|lng_jkm|lng_ttf — promote to reference product]']
  scheduled_lifting_date date [note: 'Planned calendar date on which the cargo lifting is scheduled to commence at the terminal or loading port, as agreed in the term offtake agreement or spot sale nomination. Used for production planning and inventory management. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category (day-level planning precision).']
  sulfur_content_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Sulfur content of the crude oil cargo expressed as a weight percentage (wt%). Classifies crude as sweet (<0.5% sulfur) or sour (>0.5% sulfur), directly impacting pricing differential, refinery processing requirements, and environmental compliance under IMO 2020 sulfur regulations.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this lifting schedule record was last modified. Tracks schedule revisions, status changes, and volume adjustments for audit and data lineage purposes. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.']
  vessel_imo_number varchar [note: 'International Maritime Organization (IMO) unique vessel identification number in the format IMO followed by 7 digits. Provides a globally unique, permanent vessel identifier for regulatory reporting, sanctions screening, and cargo tracking.']
  volume_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for all volume fields on this lifting record. BBL (barrels) is standard for crude oil and condensate; MT (metric tonnes) is standard for LNG and some crude trades; MMBTU for gas energy content; MCF for gas volume. Ensures consistent interpretation of entitlement and actual volume fields.']
  volume_variance decimal(18,4) [note: 'Difference between actual_lifted_volume and entitlement_volume, expressed in the unit defined by volume_unit. Positive value indicates over-lift; negative value indicates under-lift. Used for production allocation reconciliation, over/under-lift accounting, and partner balancing under JOA terms.']

  Note: 'Planned and actual lifting schedule for a customer account against a term offtake agreement or spot sale, capturing lifting number, scheduled lifting date, actual lifting date, product, volume entitlement (BBL or MT), actual lifted volume, terminal or loading port, vessel, bill of lading number, lifting status (scheduled, in-progress, completed, deferred), and variance from plan. Supports production allocation, inventory management, and revenue recognition for crude oil and LNG liftings.'
}

  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Settlement payments, credit notes, and warranty claims post to specific GL accounts (customer claims expense, sales returns). Required for accurate revenue recognition and expense matching.']

  petroleum_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Complaints reference specific petroleum products with quality issues (off-spec sulfur, contamination, wrong grade delivered). Quality management and root cause analysis require linking complaints to p']

Business justification: Complaints frequently reference specific sales orders for product quality, delivery, or invoicing issues. Business process: root cause analysis, vendor performance impact']

  communication_channel varchar [note: 'Channel through which the complaint was originally submitted by the customer. Telex is included as it remains in use for formal maritime and cargo communications in the oil and gas industry. Supports channel analytics and intake process optimization.']
  complaint_category varchar [note: 'Primary classification of the complaint type. Drives routing to the appropriate resolution team and root cause analysis framework. Categories align with oil and gas commercial operations: product_quality (off-spec crude/products), short_delivery (volume shortfall), invoice_dispute (billing error), vessel_delay (FPSO/tanker scheduling), documentation_error (bill of lading, COA), pricing_discrepancy (WTI/Brent differential disputes).']

  customer_satisfaction_score varchar [note: 'Numeric satisfaction rating provided by the customer following resolution, typically on a scale of 1 to 10. Complements the qualitative customer_satisfaction_outcome field. Used for KPI reporting and account health monitoring.']
  delivery_reference varchar [note: 'Outbound delivery or bill of lading number associated with the complaint. Distinct from cargo_reference in that it represents the logistics execution document rather than the commercial cargo nomination.']
  escalation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the complaint has been formally escalated to senior management or a specialist team. True when escalation_owner_id is populated and formal escalation process has been triggered.']
  hse_incident_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number of the associated HSE incident record in Enablon HSE Management system, when the complaint has triggered a parallel safety or environmental incident investigation. Null when hse_related is False.']
  hse_related boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the complaint has an associated Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) implication, such as a product quality issue involving H2S content, NORM contamination, or a delivery incident with environmental impact. Triggers parallel HSE incident workflow in Enablon.']

Triggers JV accounting and partner notification workflows.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent modification to the complaint record in the data platform. Used for incremental data loading, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance. Supports SOX compliance and data governance.']
  receipt_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time at which the complaint was received and registered in the system. Used for SLA clock start and audit trail purposes. Distinct from complaint_date which captures the business event date.']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally communicated complaint reference number shared with the customer for tracking purposes. Follows the format COMP-YYYY-NNNNNN. Used in all customer-facing correspondence and SAP SD service notification references.']
  regulatory_body_notified varchar [note: 'Name of the regulatory authority notified in connection with the complaint (e.g., EPA, BSEE, PHMSA, FERC). Populated only when regulatory_notification_required is True. Supports regulatory compliance audit trail.']
  regulatory_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the complaint involves a matter requiring notification to a regulatory body (e.g., EPA for environmental product quality issues, BSEE for offshore delivery failures, PHMSA for pipeline delivery incidents). Triggers compliance workflow in Enablon HSE Management.']
  repeat_complaint boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this complaint represents a recurrence of a previously resolved complaint from the same customer for the same root cause or issue type. Signals ineffective corrective action and triggers enhanced investigation under continuous improvement protocols.']
  resolution_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative of the actions taken to resolve the complaint, including investigation findings, corrective measures applied, and any commercial settlement agreed. Classified confidential due to commercially sensitive content.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the identified root cause of the complaint. Supports systemic trend analysis and continuous improvement programs. process_failure: upstream or downstream process deviation; equipment_failure: metering, pumping, or vessel equipment; human_error: operational or administrative error; supplier_issue: third-party or JV partner failure; logistics_failure: transportation or scheduling failure; measurement_error: API MPMS measurement discrepancy.']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative of the identified root cause following investigation. Provides specific technical or operational context beyond the root_cause_category classification. Used for corrective action planning and lessons learned documentation.']
  severity varchar [note: 'Business impact severity rating assigned at intake or triage. Critical: potential regulatory breach, HSE implication, or major commercial loss. High: significant financial impact or key account at risk. Medium: moderate operational impact. Low: minor administrative issue. Drives SLA target assignment and escalation thresholds.']
  sla_breached boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the complaint resolution exceeded the target resolution date, constituting an SLA breach. True when actual_resolution_date exceeds target_resolution_date or when complaint remains open past target date. Drives management reporting and continuous improvement.']
  source_system_reference varchar [note: 'Original system identifier or notification number from the operational system of record (e.g., SAP SD service notification number, CRM case ID) from which this complaint record was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation with upstream systems.']
  subcategory varchar [note: 'Secondary classification providing granular detail within the complaint category.   target_resolution_date date [note: 'Contractually or operationally committed date by which the complaint must be resolved. Derived from complaint severity and SLA policy. Used for SLA breach monitoring and escalation triggering.']

  Note: 'Formal customer complaint record capturing complaint reference, complaint date, complaint category (product quality, short delivery, invoice dispute, vessel delay, documentation error, pricing discrepancy), affected product, affected cargo or delivery, complaint description, severity, assigned resolution owner, target resolution date, actual resolution date, resolution description, root cause, and customer satisfaction outcome. Supports customer service management and continuous improvement.'

Table customer.sanctions_screening {
  sanctions_screening_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each sanctions screening event record. Primary key for the sanctions_screening data product in the customer domain. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete compliance event with its own lifecycle, timestamps, party reference, and outcome.']
  account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Sanctions screening can be account-specific, not just counterparty-level. Accounts may require separate screening based on their specific commercial activities, jurisdictions, or transaction patterns.']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Sanctions screening, compliance monitoring, and regulatory reporting costs are allocated to legal/compliance cost centers for overhead tracking and compliance program cost management.']
  customer_counterparty_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the counterparty or customer record that was screened. Links the sanctions screening event to the master customer/counterparty entity (IOC, NOC, refiner, trader, wholesale buyer, industrial consumer, retail distributor, or contract counterparty). Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the compliance officer or authorized reviewer who reviewed the screening result and recorded the disposition decision. Links to the workforce/employee master for accountability and audit trail purposes.']
  kyc_record_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the KYC record associated with this counterparty at the time of screening. Links the sanctions screening event to the broader KYC compliance record for integrated AML/sanctions risk management. Supports cross-referencing between sanctions screening outcomes and KYC status.']
  venture_partner_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to venture.partner. Business justification: Sanctions screening of venture partners in their customer capacity is required for commercial transactions. Critical for OFAC/EU/UN sanctions compliance, partner transaction screening, regulatory repo']
  adverse_media_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether adverse media (negative news) was identified for this counterparty during the screening event, such as reports of corruption, bribery, sanctions violations, or involvement in illicit activities. Adverse media findings may trigger enhanced due diligence or re-screening.']
  blocking_action_taken boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a blocking action was executed as a result of this screening event, such as freezing assets, blocking a transaction, or suspending the counterparty account in accordance with OFAC or applicable sanctions authority requirements.']
  compliance_officer_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by the compliance officer documenting the rationale for the disposition decision, investigation findings, or escalation justification. Retained as part of the regulatory audit record.']
  counterparty_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the counterparty\'s country of incorporation or primary operations at the time of screening. Used for jurisdiction risk assessment and country-level sanctions embargo checks (e.g., Iran, Russia, North Korea, Cuba, Syria).']
  counterparty_name_screened varchar [note: 'The exact legal name of the counterparty as submitted to the sanctions screening engine at the time of screening. This may differ from the current master record name if the entity has undergone a name change, ensuring a point-in-time audit record of what was screened.']
  counterparty_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the counterparty being screened by their commercial relationship type with Oil Gas. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ioc|noc|refiner|trader|wholesale_buyer|industrial_consumer|retail_distributor|contract_counterparty — promote to reference product]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this sanctions screening record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.']
  disposition varchar [note: 'The final compliance disposition assigned to this screening event following human review. \'cleared\' = reviewed and confirmed not a sanctions match; \'escalated\' = referred to senior compliance or legal counsel; \'blocked\' = counterparty blocked from transacting; \'pending_review\' = awaiting compliance officer decision; \'false_positive\' = confirmed algorithmic false positive, no action required.']
  disposition_date date [note: 'The date on which the compliance officer or authorized reviewer recorded the final disposition decision for this screening event. Required for regulatory audit trails and SLA compliance tracking.']
  escalation_reason varchar [note: 'Documented reason for escalating this screening event to senior compliance, legal counsel, or management. Applicable when disposition is \'escalated\'. Examples: \'Confirmed SDN match\', \'Beneficial owner PEP identified\', \'Jurisdiction under OFAC comprehensive sanctions\', \'Unresolved potential match above threshold\'.']
  eu_consolidated_list_checked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the EU Consolidated List of Persons, Groups, and Entities Subject to EU Financial Sanctions was included in this screening event. Required for EU-nexus counterparties and transactions under EU Regulation 2580/2001 and related Council Regulations.']
  hm_treasury_list_checked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the UK HM Treasury Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) Consolidated List was included in this screening event. Required for UK-nexus counterparties and transactions post-Brexit under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018.']
  jurisdiction_risk_level varchar [note: 'Risk classification of the counterparty\'s jurisdiction at the time of screening, based on FATF country risk ratings, OFAC country-based sanctions programs, and internal country risk policy. \'prohibited\' = country subject to comprehensive sanctions embargo (e.g., Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria).']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this sanctions screening record was last modified, such as when a disposition decision was recorded or a compliance officer updated the outcome. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.']
  license_exemption_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier for any OFAC specific license, EU derogation, or other regulatory exemption that authorizes a transaction with a sanctioned or potentially sanctioned counterparty. Null if no license or exemption applies. Critical for documenting authorized exceptions.']
  list_version_date date [note: 'The publication or effective date of the sanctions list versions used during this screening event. Ensures the audit record captures which version of the lists was current at the time of screening, critical for demonstrating due diligence.']
  match_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Algorithmic confidence score (0.00–100.00) produced by the sanctions screening engine indicating the degree of similarity between the screened counterparty and a listed entity. Scores above the configured threshold trigger a \'potential_match\' or \'match\' result requiring human review. Used for risk-based triage and audit documentation.']
  match_threshold_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The minimum algorithmic match score percentage configured in the screening engine at the time of this screening event that triggers a \'potential_match\' result requiring human review. Retained for audit purposes to document the sensitivity of the screening methodology applied.']
  matched_entity_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier assigned to the matched entity on the relevant sanctions list (e.g., OFAC SDN UID, EU list reference number, UN reference number). Null if no match. Used for precise cross-referencing with regulatory list databases.']
  matched_entity_name varchar [note: 'The name of the sanctioned entity or individual on the screening list that was matched or potentially matched against the counterparty. Null if screening_result is \'clear\'. Retained for audit trail and regulatory reporting purposes.']
  matched_list_name varchar [note: 'Name of the specific sanctions list on which a match or potential match was identified (e.g., \'OFAC SDN\', \'EU Consolidated\', \'UN Security Council\', \'HM Treasury OFSI\'). Null if screening_result is \'clear\'. Critical for compliance officer investigation and regulatory reporting.']
  next_screening_due_date date [note: 'The scheduled date by which the next periodic sanctions screening must be completed for this counterparty, calculated based on the counterparty\'s risk tier and screening frequency policy. Drives the compliance calendar and automated screening workflow.']
  ofac_sdn_list_checked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List was included in this screening event. Mandatory for all US-nexus transactions and counterparties under 31 CFR Part 501.']
  pep_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the counterparty or any of its beneficial owners has been identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) during this screening event. PEP status elevates the counterparty\'s risk profile and may require enhanced due diligence under FATF Recommendation 12.']
  regulatory_report_date date [note: 'The date on which the mandatory regulatory report was submitted to the relevant sanctions authority. Null if regulatory_reporting_required is False or report has not yet been submitted. Critical for demonstrating timely compliance with reporting deadlines.']
  regulatory_report_submitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the required regulatory report has been submitted to the relevant authority (e.g., OFAC, EU competent authority, OFSI). Applicable only when regulatory_reporting_required is True. Used to track compliance with mandatory reporting deadlines.']
  regulatory_reporting_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this sanctions screening event triggers a mandatory regulatory reporting obligation (e.g., OFAC blocked property report, SAR filing, EU competent authority notification). True = reporting required; False = no reporting obligation. Drives downstream compliance workflow.']
  review_completed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the compliance officer completed their review and recorded the final disposition for this screening event. Used to measure review turnaround time against internal SLA targets and regulatory timeliness requirements.']
  screening_engine varchar [note: 'Name and version of the sanctions screening software or service used to execute this screening event (e.g., \'Dow Jones Watchlist\', \'Refinitiv World-Check\', \'LexisNexis Bridger\', \'Accuity Firco\'). Required for audit trail and to assess screening methodology adequacy.']
  screening_frequency_code varchar [note: 'The scheduled screening frequency applicable to this counterparty based on their risk tier and compliance policy. Determines the cadence for periodic re-screening. \'daily\' = continuous monitoring for highest-risk counterparties; \'annual\' = lowest-risk counterparties.']
  screening_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business identifier assigned to this screening event, used for audit trails, regulatory correspondence, and compliance officer tracking. Format: SCR-{YYYY}-{8-digit sequence}. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.']
  screening_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of the automated sanctions list matching process. \'clear\' = no match found on any screened list; \'match\' = confirmed match against a sanctioned entity; \'potential_match\' = algorithmic hit requiring human review; \'inconclusive\' = insufficient data to determine match status. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category (non-monetary compliance event).']
  screening_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the sanctions screening event workflow. \'pending\' = queued for screening; \'in_progress\' = screening underway; \'completed\' = screening concluded with a disposition; \'escalated\' = referred to senior compliance officer or legal; \'cancelled\' = screening voided. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.']
  screening_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time at which the sanctions screening was executed against the applicable screening lists. This is the principal real-world event time for the screening transaction, distinct from record creation. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.']
  screening_trigger_event varchar [note: 'Description of the specific business event that triggered this screening, particularly for \'triggered\' and \'ad_hoc\' screening types. Examples: \'New contract execution\', \'Ownership change notification\', \'Adverse media alert\', \'Country risk upgrade\', \'Credit limit increase\', \'Joint venture partner addition\'.']
  screening_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the screening event by its business trigger. \'onboarding\' = initial screening at counterparty onboarding; \'periodic\' = scheduled recurring review; \'triggered\' = event-driven re-screening (e.g., adverse media, ownership change, country risk change); \'ad_hoc\' = manual compliance officer request; \'renewal\' = screening at contract or credit renewal.']
  source_system_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier or reference number from the originating operational system that initiated or recorded this sanctions screening event (e.g., Enablon HSE Management compliance module reference, SAP S/4HANA vendor master screening reference, or KYC workflow system reference). Supports data lineage and cross-system reconciliation.']

  makeup_period_days varchar [note: 'The number of days following the end of the commitment period during which the customer may make up shortfall volumes from a prior period without incurring the shortfall penalty.   makeup_volume_available decimal(18,4) [note: 'The remaining volume the customer is entitled to lift as make-up against previously paid shortfall penalties, expressed in volume_uom. Tracks the outstanding make-up entitlement balance that has not yet been exercised within the make-up period.']

  min_committed_volume decimal(18,4) [note: 'The minimum volume the customer is contractually obligated to take or pay for during the commitment period, expressed in the unit of measure defined by volume_uom. This is the take-or-pay (TOP) floor quantity. Failure to lift this volume triggers shortfall penalty calculations.']
  nomination_deadline_days varchar [note: 'The number of calendar days prior to the delivery period start by which the customer must submit a volume nomination to the seller. Governs the commercial scheduling process and determines the latest date for volume scheduling in the supply chain.']
  price_index_reference varchar [note: 'The benchmark price index to which the committed volume pricing is linked when pricing_basis is \'index_linked\' or \'spot_differential\' (e.g., WTI NYMEX, Brent ICE, Henry Hub NYMEX, Platts Dated Brent). Used for invoice calculation and revenue forecasting.']
  pricing_basis varchar [note: 'The pricing mechanism governing the commercial value of volumes delivered under this commitment. \'fixed\' = agreed fixed price per unit; \'index_linked\' = tied to a benchmark index (e.g., WTI, Brent, Henry Hub); \'formula\' = calculated via a contractual formula; \'spot_differential\' = spot price plus/minus a negotiated differential.']
  renewal_notice_days varchar [note: 'The number of calendar days prior to the commitment expiry date by which the customer must provide written notice to exercise the renewal option. Populated only when renewal_option_flag is True. Supports contract expiry management and commercial relationship planning.']
  renewal_option_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the term supply agreement governing this commitment includes a renewal option that the customer may exercise at or before the effective_until date. True = renewal option exists; False = no renewal option. Supports commercial contract lifecycle management and revenue forecasting.']
  shortfall_penalty_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'The contractual penalty rate applied per unit of shortfall volume when the customer fails to meet the minimum committed volume (take-or-pay obligation). Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code per volume_uom unit. Used to calculate the shortfall penalty invoice amount.']
  shortfall_volume decimal(18,4) [note: 'The volume by which the customer\'s actual deliveries fall short of the minimum committed volume at the end of the commitment period, expressed in volume_uom. Calculated as max(0, min_committed_volume - delivered_volume_to_date). A positive value triggers shortfall penalty invoicing.']
  take_or_pay_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The take-or-pay (TOP) percentage of the maximum contracted volume that the customer must either lift or pay for during the commitment period. For example, 80% means the customer must take or pay for at least 80% of the maximum contracted volume. Used to derive the minimum committed volume when expressed as a percentage.']
  tolerance_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The contractually permitted percentage variance (plus or minus) around the nominated or committed volume within which actual deliveries are considered compliant without triggering shortfall or excess penalties.   volume_escalation_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The contractually agreed annual percentage by which the minimum committed volume escalates (or de-escalates if negative) from one contract year to the next.   Note: 'Customer volume commitment record under a term supply agreement, capturing commitment period (annual, quarterly, monthly), minimum committed volume (BBL, MT, MMBTU), maximum contracted volume, take-or-pay obligation, make-up period, product grade, delivery point, actual delivered volume to date, shortfall volume, shortfall penalty rate, and commitment status.   role_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the counterparty\'s commercial role in relation to the JOA. OFFTAKER indicates the counterparty purchases production; SUPPLIER provides goods or services; MARKETING_AGENT handles sales; REFINING_PARTNER processes crude; TRANSPORTATION_PROVIDER handles logistics']

  Note: 'This association product represents the commercial participation relationship between customer counterparties and Joint Operating Agreements. It captures commercial offtake arrangements, pricing elections, and participation terms for counterparties who are commercial buyers or sellers under a JOA, distinct from working interest partners. Each record links one customer counterparty to one JOA with attributes that exist only in the context of this commercial relationship.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas joint ventures, a single counterparty (e.g., a refiner or trader) can have commercial offtake or supply arrangements with multiple JOAs across different assets, and each JOA typically has multiple commercial counterparties beyond the working interest partners (offtakers, refiners, marketers, transporters). These commercial participation arrangements are actively managed operational relationships with specific terms, pricing elections, volume entitlements, and status tracking that belong to the relationship itself, not to either the counterparty master record or the JOA governance document.'
}
